post.title: Card fraud: why debit can drain your checking account
post.ig:
Same fraud, two cards. Only one drains your checking account.

Credit card: the Truth in Lending Act caps what you owe for unauthorized charges at $50, and under Regulation Z you don't have to pay a disputed charge while it's investigated.
Debit card: under Regulation E the bank has 10 business days to decide, or it can provisionally credit you and take up to 45 days (90 for some debit purchases).
Example: $2,500 in checking - $2,000 stolen = $500 left while you wait, so autopays can bounce and overdraft fees can hit.
Card networks' zero-liability policies often cover debit too; the gap is whose money is missing during the investigation.

Sources: 12 CFR 1026.12 and 1026.13 (Regulation Z), 12 CFR 1005.11 (Regulation E), CFPB, FTC.
